subject: math
title: Grade 9 Adding and Subtracting Polynomials
seo_title: Grade 9 Adding and Subtracting Polynomials Worksheets: Like Terms and Algebra Tiles (Free, Answer Key, BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Operations with polynomials, of degree less than or equal to 2
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 math worksheets on adding and subtracting polynomials for the BC curriculum: terms, degree and like terms, algebra tiles and zero pairs, adding polynomials, subtracting by changing every sign, and perimeter word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Combine only like terms, and keep the exponents: 3x² + 5x² = 8x², and x + x = 2x, not x².
key_sub: To subtract, change the sign of every term in the second polynomial, then add: (5x² + 3x − 4) − (2x² − x + 6) = 3x² + 4x − 10.
body_html:
Terms, degree and like terms

A polynomial is a sum of terms such as 3x2 − 2x + 5. Each sign belongs to the term after it, so the terms are 3x2, −2x and 5. One term is a monomial, two terms a binomial and three terms a trinomial.

The degree is the greatest exponent: 3x2 − 2x + 5 has degree 2. Like terms have the same variable with the same exponent, such as 4x2 and −x2. Only like terms can be combined.

ExpressionAdd the coefficientsResult
3x + 5x3 + 5 = 88x
4x2 − x24 − 1 = 33x2
3x2 + 2xnot like terms3x2 + 2x

Algebra tiles

Add polynomials

Remove the brackets, group like terms, and add the coefficients. The exponents do not change.

Example 1

Add (4 + 3x − x2) + (2x2 − 5 + x).

Match like terms even when the order is different. x2-terms: −1 + 2 = 1. x-terms: 3 + 1 = 4. Constants: 4 + (−5) = −1.

Answer: x2 + 4x − 1

Subtract polynomials

To subtract, add the opposite: change the sign of every term in the second polynomial, then add.

Example 2

Subtract (5x2 + 3x − 4) − (2x2 − x + 6).

(5x2 + 3x − 4) − (2x2 − x + 6) = (5x2 + 3x − 4) + (−2x2 + x − 6). x2-terms: 5 + (−2) = 3. x-terms: 3 + 1 = 4. Constants: −4 + (−6) = −10.

Answer: 3x2 + 4x − 10

Perimeter

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
x + x = x2x + x = 2x. x2 means x × x
3x2 + 2x = 5x23x2 and 2x are not like terms, so they stay apart
(5x2 + 3x − 4) − (2x2 − x + 6) = 3x2 + 2x + 2Change every sign: −2x2 + x − 6, so the answer is 3x2 + 4x − 10
“Subtract A from B” written as A − BIt means B − A
Adding only two sides for a perimeterAdd every side of the shape

faq.q: What do Grade 9 students learn about polynomials in the BC math curriculum?
faq.a: The Mathematics 9 Patterning standard covers operations with polynomials of degree 2 or less. Students often start with algebra tiles, then add and subtract polynomials such as (2x² − x + 3) + (x² + 3x − 1) by combining like terms.
Change the sign of every term in the second polynomial, then add like terms. For (5x² + 3x − 4) − (2x² − x + 6), write 5x² + 3x − 4 − 2x² + x − 6 = 3x² + 4x − 10.

faq.q: Why is x + x equal to 2x and not x²?
faq.a: x + x means two x’s, so it is 2x. x² means x × x. When x = 3, x + x = 6 but x² = 9, so they are not the same.

faq.q: What is the degree of a polynomial?
faq.a: It is the greatest exponent on the variable in any term. 5x² + 3x − 1 has degree 2, 7x − 4 has degree 1, and a constant such as −6 has degree 0.

items.q: Which polynomial is a binomial?
items.e: A binomial has two terms. 4x − 9 has the terms 4x and −9. (x2 + 4x − 9 has three terms.)

items.q: Which polynomial is a trinomial?
items.e: A trinomial has three terms: 2x2, −x and 5. (2x2 − 5 has only two terms.)

items.q: Which polynomial is a monomial?
items.e: A monomial has one term. −7x2 is one term: the minus sign is part of the coefficient. (7 − x2 is two terms.)

items.q: How many terms does 6x2 − 5x + 1 have?
items.e: The terms are 6x2, −5x and 1. Each + or − sign starts a new term, so there are 3 terms. (2 counts the signs instead of the terms.)

items.q: What is the degree of 5x2 + 3x − 1?
items.e: The degree is the greatest exponent on the variable. 5x2 has exponent 2, so the degree is 2. (5 is a coefficient. 3 is the number of terms.)

items.q: What is the degree of 7x − 4?
items.e: 7x means 7x1, so the greatest exponent is 1. The degree is 1. (2 is the number of terms.)

items.q: What is the degree of −6?
items.e: A constant has no variable. You can think of it as −6x0, so the degree is 0. (−6 is the value, not the degree.)

items.q: What is the degree of 4xy + 3x?
items.e: For a term with two variables, add their exponents: xy = x1y1, so 1 + 1 = 2. The degree is 2. (1 looks only at the exponent of x.)

items.q: What is the degree of 3 + 2x − x2?
items.e: Look at every term, not only the first one. −x2 has exponent 2, so the degree is 2. (0 uses only the first term, 3.)

items.q: What is the coefficient of x in 3x2 − x + 8?
items.e: −x means −1x, so the coefficient is −1. The sign belongs to the term after it. (0 forgets that x on its own is 1x.)

items.q: What is the constant term of 2x2 + 5x − 9?
items.e: The constant term has no variable: −9. Keep the minus sign in front of it. (9 drops the sign.)

items.q: What is the coefficient of x2 in 4 − 7x2 + x?
items.e: The x2-term is −7x2, so the coefficient is −7. (2 is the exponent, not the coefficient. 4 is the constant term.)

items.q: Which term is a like term with 3x2?
items.e: Like terms have the same variable with the same exponent. −5x2 and 3x2 both have x2. (3x has exponent 1. 3y2 has a different variable.)

items.q: Which pair are like terms?
items.e: −2x and 9x both have x to the exponent 1, so they are like terms. The coefficients can be different. (4x and 4x2 have different exponents.)

items.q: Which term is a like term with 7xy?
items.e: yx is the same as xy, because the order of multiplying does not matter. So −2yx is a like term with 7xy. (7x has no y.)

items.q: Leah says x + x = x2. Which statement is correct?
items.e: x + x is two x’s, so it is 2x. Test with x = 3: x + x = 6, but x2 = 9. x2 means x × x.

items.q: Simplify 3x + 5x.
items.e: Add the coefficients and keep the variable: 3 + 5 = 8, so 8x. (8x2 uses x + x = x2.)

items.q: Simplify 4x2 + 2x2 − x2.
items.e: Add the coefficients: 4 + 2 − 1 = 5. The exponent does not change: 5x2. (5x6 adds the exponents. 7x2 ignores the minus sign.)

items.q: Simplify 2x2 + 3x + 5x2 − 7x.
items.e: x2-terms: 2 + 5 = 7. x-terms: 3 − 7 = −4. The answer is 7x2 − 4x. (3x2 joins unlike terms. 7x4 − 4x2 uses x + x = x2.)

items.q: Simplify x2 − 3x + 4 − 4x2 + x − 6.
items.e: x2-terms: 1 − 4 = −3. x-terms: −3 + 1 = −2. Constants: 4 − 6 = −2. The answer is −3x2 − 2x − 2. (5x2 ignores the minus sign of 4x2. −7 joins unlike terms.)

items.q: Blue tiles are x2, green tiles are x and yellow tiles are 1. Red tiles are negative. Which polynomial do the tiles show?
items.e: 2 blue tiles, 3 green tiles and 2 yellow tiles: 2x2 + 3x + 2. (3x2 + 2x + 2 mixes up the large square and the long tiles.)

items.q: Blue tiles are x2, green tiles are x and yellow tiles are 1. Red tiles are negative. Which polynomial do the tiles show?
items.e: 1 blue tile, 4 red x-tiles and 3 yellow tiles: x2 − 4x + 3. (x2 + 4x + 3 counts the red tiles as positive.)

items.q: Blue tiles are x2, green tiles are x and yellow tiles are 1. Red tiles are negative. Which polynomial do the tiles show?
items.e: 2 red x2-tiles give −2x2. 1 green tile gives x. 1 yellow and 1 red 1-tile make a zero pair, so 3 red 1-tiles are left: −3. The tiles show −2x2 + x − 3. (−2x2 + x − 4 forgets the yellow tile.)

items.q: Blue tiles are x2, green tiles are x and yellow tiles are 1. Red tiles are negative. Which polynomial do the tiles show?
items.e: x2-tiles: 3 blue and 1 red leave 2x2. x-tiles: 2 green and 3 red leave −x. 1-tiles: 2 yellow and 1 red leave 1. The tiles show 2x2 − x + 1. (4x2 + 5x + 3 counts the red tiles as positive.)

items.q: Blue tiles are x2, green tiles are x and yellow tiles are 1. Red tiles are negative. Which polynomial do the tiles show?
items.e: The 3 yellow and 3 red 1-tiles are 3 zero pairs, so they make 0. The tiles show x2 − 2x. (−x joins x2 and −2x, which are not like terms.)

items.q: Blue tiles are x2, green tiles are x and yellow tiles are 1. Red tiles are negative. Remove all the zero pairs. How many tiles are left?
items.e: There is 1 zero pair of x2-tiles, 1 of x-tiles and 1 of 1-tiles: 3 pairs, or 6 tiles. 10 − 6 = 4 tiles are left, which show x2 + 2x − 1. (6 is the number of tiles removed. 7 removes only one tile from each pair.)

items.q: Blue tiles are x2, green tiles are x and yellow tiles are 1. Red tiles are negative. The tiles show (x2 + 2x + 1) + (x2 + x + 3). What is the sum?
items.e: Group the tiles of the same kind and remove zero pairs. x2-terms: 1 + 1 = 2. x-terms: 2 + 1 = 3. Constants: 1 + 3 = 4. The sum is 2x2 + 3x + 4. (2x4 + 3x2 + 4 uses x + x = x2.)

items.q: Blue tiles are x2, green tiles are x and yellow tiles are 1. Red tiles are negative. The tiles show (2x2 − x + 3) + (x2 + 3x − 1). What is the sum?
items.e: Group the tiles of the same kind and remove zero pairs. x2-terms: 2 + 1 = 3. x-terms: −1 + 3 = 2. Constants: 3 + (−1) = 2. The sum is 3x2 + 2x + 2. (3x4 + 2x2 + 2 uses x + x = x2.)

items.q: Blue tiles are x2, green tiles are x and yellow tiles are 1. Red tiles are negative. The tiles show (−x2 + 2x − 2) + (2x2 + x + 4). What is the sum?
items.e: Group the tiles of the same kind and remove zero pairs. x2-terms: −1 + 2 = 1. x-terms: 2 + 1 = 3. Constants: −2 + 4 = 2. The sum is x2 + 3x + 2. (x4 + 3x2 + 2 uses x + x = x2.)

items.q: Blue tiles are x2, green tiles are x and yellow tiles are 1. Red tiles are negative. The tiles show (x2 − 3x) + (−x2 + x + 2). What is the sum?
items.e: Group the tiles of the same kind and remove zero pairs. x2-terms: 1 + (−1) = 0. x-terms: −3 + 1 = −2. Constants: 0 + 2 = 2. The sum is −2x + 2. (−2x2 + 2 uses x + x = x2.)

items.q: Blue tiles are x2, green tiles are x and yellow tiles are 1. Red tiles are negative. The tiles show (2x2 + x − 3) + (−x2 − 2x + 1). What is the sum?
items.e: Group the tiles of the same kind and remove zero pairs. x2-terms: 2 + (−1) = 1. x-terms: 1 + (−2) = −1. Constants: −3 + 1 = −2. The sum is x2 − x − 2. (x4 − x2 − 2 uses x + x = x2.)

items.q: Blue tiles are x2, green tiles are x and yellow tiles are 1. Red tiles are negative. The tiles show (3x − 2) + (x2 − x − 2). What is the sum?
items.e: Group the tiles of the same kind and remove zero pairs. x2-terms: 0 + 1 = 1. x-terms: 3 + (−1) = 2. Constants: −2 + (−2) = −4. The sum is x2 + 2x − 4. (3x2 − 4 uses x + x = x2.)

items.q: Blue tiles are x2, green tiles are x and yellow tiles are 1. Red tiles are negative. The tiles show (−2x2 + 3) + (3x2 − 2x − 1). What is the sum?
items.e: Group the tiles of the same kind and remove zero pairs. x2-terms: −2 + 3 = 1. x-terms: 0 + (−2) = −2. Constants: 3 + (−1) = 2. The sum is x2 − 2x + 2. (x4 − 2x + 2 uses x + x = x2.)

items.q: Blue tiles are x2, green tiles are x and yellow tiles are 1. Red tiles are negative. Which polynomial is the opposite of the polynomial shown? (Together they make zero.)
items.e: To make zero, flip every tile to the other colour, so change the sign of every term: the opposite of x2 + 2x − 3 is −x2 − 2x + 3. (−x2 + 2x − 3 changes only the first sign.)

items.q: Blue tiles are x2, green tiles are x and yellow tiles are 1. Red tiles are negative. Which polynomial is the opposite of the polynomial shown? (Together they make zero.)
items.e: To make zero, flip every tile to the other colour, so change the sign of every term: the opposite of −2x2 + x + 4 is 2x2 − x − 4. (2x2 + x + 4 changes only the first sign.)

items.q: Blue tiles are x2, green tiles are x and yellow tiles are 1. Red tiles are negative. The tiles show (3x2 + 4x + 5) − (x2 + 2x + 1): the crossed-out tiles are taken away. What is the difference?
items.e: Count the tiles that are left. x2-terms: 3 + (−1) = 2. x-terms: 4 + (−2) = 2. Constants: 5 + (−1) = 4. The difference is 2x2 + 2x + 4. (2x2 + 6x + 6 changes only the sign of the first term.)

items.q: Blue tiles are x2, green tiles are x and yellow tiles are 1. Red tiles are negative. The tiles show (2x2 − 3x + 4) − (x2 − 2x + 1): the crossed-out tiles are taken away. What is the difference?
items.e: Count the tiles that are left. x2-terms: 2 + (−1) = 1. x-terms: −3 + 2 = −1. Constants: 4 + (−1) = 3. The difference is x2 − x + 3. (x2 − 5x + 5 changes only the sign of the first term.)

items.q: Blue tiles are x2, green tiles are x and yellow tiles are 1. Red tiles are negative. The tiles show (x2 + 2x) − (−x). Zero pairs were added, then the crossed-out tiles were taken away. What is the difference?
items.e: There is no red x-tile to take away, so add a zero pair (x and −x). Take away the red tile: x2 + 2x − (−x) = x2 + 3x. Subtracting a negative is the same as adding. (x2 + x subtracts x instead.)

items.q: Blue tiles are x2, green tiles are x and yellow tiles are 1. Red tiles are negative. The tiles show (x2 − 2x + 3) − (−x2). Zero pairs were added, then the crossed-out tiles were taken away. What is the difference?
items.e: Add a zero pair of x2-tiles, then take away the red one. 2 blue tiles are left: x2 − 2x + 3 − (−x2) = 2x2 − 2x + 3. (−2x + 3 subtracts x2 instead of adding it.)

items.q: Blue tiles are x2, green tiles are x and yellow tiles are 1. Red tiles are negative. The tiles show (3x + 2) − (x + 4). Zero pairs were added, then the crossed-out tiles were taken away. What is the difference?
items.e: Start with 3x + 2. To take away 4 yellow tiles, add 2 zero pairs of 1-tiles first. Take away 1 green tile and 4 yellow tiles: 2 green and 2 red tiles are left, 2x − 2. (2x + 2 subtracts 2 from 4 instead of 4 from 2.)
x-terms: 4 + 2 = 6. Constants: 7 + (−3) = 4. The sum is 6x + 4. (6x2 + 4 uses x + x = x2, but x + x = 2x.)
x2-terms: 3 + 1 = 4. x-terms: 2 + 5 = 7. The sum is 4x2 + 7x. (4x4 + 7x2 uses x + x = x2, but x + x = 2x.)
x2-terms: 2 + 4 = 6. x-terms: −5 + 3 = −2. Constants: 1 + 6 = 7. The sum is 6x2 − 2x + 7. (6x4 − 2x2 + 7 uses x + x = x2, but x + x = 2x.)
x2-terms: 1 + 1 = 2. x-terms: 6 + (−2) = 4. Constants: −4 + (−5) = −9. The sum is 2x2 + 4x − 9. (2x4 + 4x2 − 9 uses x + x = x2, but x + x = 2x.)
x2-terms: −3 + 5 = 2. x-terms: 1 + (−4) = −3. Constants: 8 + (−2) = 6. The sum is 2x2 − 3x + 6. (2x4 − 3x2 + 6 uses x + x = x2, but x + x = 2x.)
x2-terms: 5 + (−2) = 3. x-terms: 0 + 7 = 7. Constants: −9 + 3 = −6. The sum is 3x2 + 7x − 6. (3x4 + 7x − 6 uses x + x = x2, but x + x = 2x.)
x2-terms: −1 + (−4) = −5. x-terms: −3 + 3 = 0. Constants: 2 + (−7) = −5. The sum is −5x2 − 5. (−5x4 − 5 uses x + x = x2, but x + x = 2x.)
x2-terms: 6 + (−6) = 0. x-terms: −2 + 5 = 3. Constants: −1 + 4 = 3. The sum is 3x + 3. (3x2 + 3 uses x + x = x2, but x + x = 2x.)
Match like terms even when they are in a different order. x2-terms: −1 + 2 = 1. x-terms: 3 + 1 = 4. Constants: 4 + (−5) = −1. The sum is x2 + 4x − 1. (x4 + 4x2 − 1 uses x + x = x2, but x + x = 2x.)
Match like terms even when they are in a different order. x2-terms: −2 + 2 = 0. x-terms: 7 + (−9) = −2. Constants: 0 + 6 = 6. The sum is −2x + 6. (−2x2 + 6 uses x + x = x2, but x + x = 2x.)
Match like terms even when they are in a different order. n2-terms: 1 + (−4) = −3. n-terms: 0 + 3 = 3. Constants: −8 + 8 = 0. The sum is −3n2 + 3n. (−3n4 + 3n uses n + n = n2, but n + n = 2n.)
x2-terms: 1 + 2 + 0 = 3. x-terms: 2 + (−1) + 4 = 5. Constants: 0 + 3 + (−5) = −2. The sum is 3x2 + 5x − 2. (8x2 − 2 uses x + x = x2, but x + x = 2x.)
x2-terms: 3 + (−1) + (−2) = 0. x-terms: 0 + 2 + (−2) = 0. Constants: −1 + 0 + 6 = 5. The sum is 5. (6x2 + 4x + 5 ignores the minus signs.)
x2-terms: 0 + 1 + 2 = 3. x-terms: 2 + (−3) + 0 = −1. Constants: 5 + 0 + (−8) = −3. The sum is 3x2 − x − 3. (3x4 − x − 3 uses x + x = x2, but x + x = 2x.)

items.q: Which polynomial must be added to 2x2 + 3x to get 5x2 − x + 4?
items.e: Subtract: (5x2 − x + 4) − (2x2 + 3x). x2-terms: 5 + (−2) = 3. x-terms: −1 + (−3) = −4. Constants: 4 + 0 = 4. Check: (2x2 + 3x) + (3x2 − 4x + 4) = 5x2 − x + 4. (7x2 + 2x + 4 adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q: Which polynomial must be added to −x2 + 4x + 6 to get x2 + 2x − 3?
items.e: Subtract: (x2 + 2x − 3) − (−x2 + 4x + 6). x2-terms: 1 + 1 = 2. x-terms: 2 + (−4) = −2. Constants: −3 + (−6) = −9. Check: (−x2 + 4x + 6) + (2x2 − 2x − 9) = x2 + 2x − 3. (6x + 3 adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q: Which polynomial must be added to 3x2 − 2x − 5 to get x + 2?
items.e: Subtract: (x + 2) − (3x2 − 2x − 5). x2-terms: 0 + (−3) = −3. x-terms: 1 + 2 = 3. Constants: 2 + 5 = 7. Check: (3x2 − 2x − 5) + (−3x2 + 3x + 7) = x + 2. (3x2 − x − 3 adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q: Ji-woo added (3x2 + 2x − 4) + (x2 + 5x + 6) and got 4x4 + 7x2 + 2. What did he do?
items.e: 3x2 + x2 = 4x2, not 4x4, and 2x + 5x = 7x, not 7x2. Adding like terms does not change the exponents. The correct sum is 4x2 + 7x + 2.

items.q: Nadia added (5x2 − 3x + 1) + (2x2 + 4x − 6) and got 7x2 + 7x − 5. What did she do?
c: She ignored the minus sign of −3x.
items.e: −3x + 4x = x, not 7x. The other terms are right: 5x2 + 2x2 = 7x2 and 1 + (−6) = −5. The correct sum is 7x2 + x − 5.

items.q: Arjun added (2x2 + 6x) + (x2 − 2x + 3) and got 3x2 + 4x + 3. What did he do?
items.e: x2-terms: 2 + 1 = 3. x-terms: 6 + (−2) = 4. Constant: 3. The sum 3x2 + 4x + 3 is correct.

items.q: Simplify −(3x2 − 2x + 5).
items.e: The minus sign in front of the brackets changes the sign of every term: −(3x2 − 2x + 5) = −3x2 + 2x − 5. (−3x2 − 2x + 5 changes only the first sign.)

items.q: Simplify −(−x2 + 4x − 6).
items.e: The minus sign in front of the brackets changes the sign of every term: −(−x2 + 4x − 6) = x2 − 4x + 6. (x2 + 4x − 6 changes only the first sign.)

items.q: Simplify −(4x2 − x − 3).
items.e: The minus sign in front of the brackets changes the sign of every term: −(4x2 − x − 3) = −4x2 + x + 3. (−4x2 − x − 3 changes only the first sign.)

Change the sign of every term in the second polynomial and add: (7x + 5) − (3x + 2) = (7x + 5) + (−3x − 2). x-terms: 7 + (−3) = 4. Constants: 5 + (−2) = 3. The difference is 4x + 3. (4x + 7 changes only the sign of the first term.)

Change the sign of every term in the second polynomial and add: (6x − 1) − (2x + 4) = (6x − 1) + (−2x − 4). x-terms: 6 + (−2) = 4. Constants: −1 + (−4) = −5. The difference is 4x − 5. (4x + 3 changes only the sign of the first term.)

items.q: Subtract: (4x2 + 3x) − (x2 − 5x)
items.e: Change the sign of every term in the second polynomial and add: (4x2 + 3x) − (x2 − 5x) = (4x2 + 3x) + (−x2 + 5x). x2-terms: 4 + (−1) = 3. x-terms: 3 + 5 = 8. The difference is 3x2 + 8x. (3x2 − 2x changes only the sign of the first term.)

items.q: Subtract: (5x2 + 3x − 4) − (2x2 − x + 6)
items.e: Change the sign of every term in the second polynomial and add: (5x2 + 3x − 4) − (2x2 − x + 6) = (5x2 + 3x − 4) + (−2x2 + x − 6). x2-terms: 5 + (−2) = 3. x-terms: 3 + 1 = 4. Constants: −4 + (−6) = −10. The difference is 3x2 + 4x − 10. (3x2 + 2x + 2 changes only the sign of the first term.)

items.q: Subtract: (2x2 − 6x + 1) − (3x2 + 2x − 5)
items.e: Change the sign of every term in the second polynomial and add: (2x2 − 6x + 1) − (3x2 + 2x − 5) = (2x2 − 6x + 1) + (−3x2 − 2x + 5). x2-terms: 2 + (−3) = −1. x-terms: −6 + (−2) = −8. Constants: 1 + 5 = 6. The difference is −x2 − 8x + 6. (−x2 − 4x − 4 changes only the sign of the first term.)

items.q: Subtract: (−x2 + 4x + 8) − (2x2 + 4x − 3)
items.e: Change the sign of every term in the second polynomial and add: (−x2 + 4x + 8) − (2x2 + 4x − 3) = (−x2 + 4x + 8) + (−2x2 − 4x + 3). x2-terms: −1 + (−2) = −3. x-terms: 4 + (−4) = 0. Constants: 8 + 3 = 11. The difference is −3x2 + 11. (−3x2 + 8x + 5 changes only the sign of the first term.)

items.q: Subtract: (3x2 − 2) − (−x2 + 5x + 7)
items.e: Change the sign of every term in the second polynomial and add: (3x2 − 2) − (−x2 + 5x + 7) = (3x2 − 2) + (x2 − 5x − 7). x2-terms: 3 + 1 = 4. x-terms: 0 + (−5) = −5. Constants: −2 + (−7) = −9. The difference is 4x2 − 5x − 9. (4x2 + 5x + 5 changes only the sign of the first term.)

items.q: Subtract: (6x2 − x) − (6x2 + 2x − 9)
items.e: Change the sign of every term in the second polynomial and add: (6x2 − x) − (6x2 + 2x − 9) = (6x2 − x) + (−6x2 − 2x + 9). x2-terms: 6 + (−6) = 0. x-terms: −1 + (−2) = −3. Constants: 0 + 9 = 9. The difference is −3x + 9. (x − 9 changes only the sign of the first term.)

Change the sign of every term in the second polynomial and add: (−4x2 + 2x − 3) − (−2x2 − 7x − 3) = (−4x2 + 2x − 3) + (2x2 + 7x + 3). x2-terms: −4 + 2 = −2. x-terms: 2 + 7 = 9. Constants: −3 + 3 = 0. The difference is −2x2 + 9x. (−2x2 − 5x − 6 changes only the sign of the first term.)

items.q: Subtract: (x2 + 8x + 2) − (−3x2 + x + 9)
items.e: Change the sign of every term in the second polynomial and add: (x2 + 8x + 2) − (−3x2 + x + 9) = (x2 + 8x + 2) + (3x2 − x − 9). x2-terms: 1 + 3 = 4. x-terms: 8 + (−1) = 7. Constants: 2 + (−9) = −7. The difference is 4x2 + 7x − 7. (4x2 + 9x + 11 changes only the sign of the first term.)

items.q: Subtract x2 + 2x from 3x2 − x + 4.
items.e: “Subtract A from B” means B − A. So work out (3x2 − x + 4) − (x2 + 2x). x2-terms: 3 + (−1) = 2. x-terms: −1 + (−2) = −3. Constants: 4 + 0 = 4. The answer is 2x2 − 3x + 4. (−2x2 + 3x − 4 subtracts in the wrong order.)

items.q: Subtract 2x2 − 3x + 5 from 4x + 1.
items.e: “Subtract A from B” means B − A. So work out (4x + 1) − (2x2 − 3x + 5). x2-terms: 0 + (−2) = −2. x-terms: 4 + 3 = 7. Constants: 1 + (−5) = −4. The answer is −2x2 + 7x − 4. (2x2 − 7x + 4 subtracts in the wrong order.)

items.q: Take −x2 + 6 away from 4x2 + 5x.
items.e: “Take A away from B” means B − A. So work out (4x2 + 5x) − (−x2 + 6). x2-terms: 4 + 1 = 5. x-terms: 5 + 0 = 5. Constants: 0 + (−6) = −6. The answer is 5x2 + 5x − 6. (−5x2 − 5x + 6 subtracts in the wrong order.)

items.q: Ryan wrote (5x2 + 3x − 4) − (2x2 − x + 6) = 3x2 + 2x + 2. What mistake did he make?
c: He changed only the sign of 2x2.
He subtracted in the wrong order.
items.e: Every sign in the second polynomial must change: −(2x2 − x + 6) = −2x2 + x − 6. Ryan kept −x and +6. The correct answer is 3x2 + 4x − 10.

items.q: Chloe wrote (4x2 − 2x + 7) − (x2 + 3x − 2) = 3x2 − 5x + 5. Which part is wrong?
items.e: −(x2 + 3x − 2) = −x2 − 3x + 2, so the constants are 7 + 2 = 9, not 7 − 2 = 5. Chloe forgot to change the sign of the last term. The correct answer is 3x2 − 5x + 9.

items.q: What must be subtracted from 4x2 + x + 3 to get x2 + 5x − 2?
items.e: (4x2 + x + 3) − ? = x2 + 5x − 2, so ? = (4x2 + x + 3) − (x2 + 5x − 2). x2-terms: 4 + (−1) = 3. x-terms: 1 + (−5) = −4. Constants: 3 + 2 = 5. Check: (4x2 + x + 3) − (3x2 − 4x + 5) = x2 + 5x − 2. (−3x2 + 4x − 5 subtracts in the wrong order.)

items.q: What must be subtracted from −2x2 + 6x to get −5x2 + 2x + 4?
Which expression gives the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: Add all four sides: (x2 + 3x) + (2x − 1) + (x2 + 3x) + (2x − 1). x2-terms: 1 + 1 = 2. x-terms: 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 = 10. Constants: −1 − 1 = −2. The perimeter is 2x2 + 10x − 2. (x2 + 5x − 1 adds only two sides. 2x2 + 8x − 1 adds only three sides.)

items.q: Which expression gives the perimeter of the triangle?
items.e: x2-terms: 1. x-terms: 1 + 2 = 3. Constants: 4 − 1 + 2 = 5. The perimeter is x2 + 3x + 5. (x2 + 3x + 7 ignores the minus sign of 1. x2 + 2x + 5 forgets that x is 1x.)

items.q: Which expression gives the perimeter of the square?
items.e: A square has 4 equal sides: (3x − 2) + (3x − 2) + (3x − 2) + (3x − 2) = 12x − 8. (12x − 2 subtracts the 2 only once. 6x − 4 adds only two sides.)

items.q: Which expression gives the perimeter of the regular hexagon?
items.e: A regular hexagon has 6 equal sides. Adding x2 + 1 six times gives 6x2 and 6 × 1 = 6: 6x2 + 6. (6x2 + 1 adds the 1 only once.)

items.q: Which expression gives the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: x2-terms: 2 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 6. x-terms: 1 + 1 = 2. Constants: −4 − 4 = −8. The perimeter is 6x2 + 2x − 8. (3x2 + x − 4 adds only two sides. 8x2 − 8 joins unlike terms.)

items.q: Which expression gives the perimeter of the trapezoid?
items.e: x2-terms: 1. x-terms: 1 + 3 + 2 = 6. Constants: 3 + 1 − 5 = −1. The perimeter is x2 + 6x − 1. (x2 + 6x + 9 ignores the minus sign of 5. 7x2 − 1 joins unlike terms.)

items.q: Which expression gives the perimeter of the triangle?
items.e: x2-terms: 1 + 1 = 2. x-terms: 1 + 1 + 3 = 5. Constant: −2. The perimeter is 2x2 + 5x − 2. (x2 + 4x − 2 adds the equal side only once.)

items.q: A rectangle has length (x2 + 3x) m and width (2x − 1) m. Its perimeter is (2x2 + 10x − 2) m. What is the perimeter when x = 4?
items.e: 2 × 4<sup>2</sup> + 10 × 4 − 2 = 32 + 40 − 2 = 70, so 70 m. (35 m adds only two sides. 74 adds the 2. 196 is length × width, the area.)

items.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 4x2 + 10x + 6. Its length is x2 + 3x + 2. Which expression gives its width?
items.e: Length + width is half the perimeter: 2x2 + 5x + 3. Width: (2x2 + 5x + 3) − (x2 + 3x + 2) = x2 + 2x + 1. (3x2 + 7x + 4 forgets to halve the perimeter.)

items.q: A triangle has a perimeter of x2 + 6x + 4. Two sides are 2x + 5 and x2 + x − 3. Which expression gives the third side?
items.e: The two sides add to x2 + 3x + 2. Third side: (x2 + 6x + 4) − (x2 + 3x + 2) = 3x + 2. (5x − 4 changes only the first sign of x2 + x − 3.)

items.q: A square has a perimeter of 8x + 12. Which expression gives the length of one side?
items.e: A square has 4 equal sides, so divide each term by 4: 8x ÷ 4 = 2x and 12 ÷ 4 = 3. Each side is 2x + 3. (2x + 12 divides only the x-term. 4x + 6 divides by 2.)

items.q: A community garden in Victoria has a perimeter of (6x2 + 4x + 2) m. A smaller garden has a perimeter of (2x2 + 4x − 6) m. How much greater is the first perimeter?
items.e: Subtract: (6x2 + 4x + 2) − (2x2 + 4x − 6) = (6x2 + 4x + 2) + (−2x2 − 4x + 6). x2-terms: 6 + (−2) = 4. x-terms: 4 + (−4) = 0. Constants: 2 + 6 = 8. The difference is (4x2 + 8) m. (4x2 − 4 forgets to change the sign of the last term.)

items.q: The school soccer field has a perimeter of (8x + 140) m. The lacrosse box has a perimeter of (6x + 60) m. How much longer is the soccer field perimeter?
items.e: (8x + 140) − (6x + 60) = 8x − 6x + 140 − 60 = 2x + 80 metres. (2x + 200 forgets to change the sign of 60.)

items.q: A Grade 9 leadership class in Surrey sells hoodies. For n hoodies, they take in 35n dollars, and the costs are (20n + 150) dollars. Which expression gives their profit?
items.e: Profit = money in − costs = 35n − (20n + 150) = 35n − 20n − 150 = 15n − 150. (15n + 150 forgets to change the sign of 150. −15n + 150 subtracts in the wrong order.)

items.q: The class’s profit is (15n − 150) dollars for n hoodies. What is the profit if they sell 40 hoodies?
items.e: 15 × 40 = 600. Then 600 − 150 = 450, so the profit is $450.00. ($750.00 adds the 150. $2350.00 uses 55n + 150, which adds the costs.)

items.q: A backyard deck in Kelowna has an area of (2x2 + 5x + 3) m2. A hot tub covers (x2 + 2x) m2 of it. Which expression gives the area of the deck that is not covered?
items.e: Subtract: (2x2 + 5x + 3) − (x2 + 2x) = (2x2 + 5x + 3) + (−x2 − 2x). x2-terms: 2 + (−1) = 1. x-terms: 5 + (−2) = 3. Constants: 3 + 0 = 3. The area is (x2 + 3x + 3) m2. (x2 + 7x + 3 changes only the sign of the first term.)

items.q: A school in Burnaby is putting new flooring in the library, with an area of (x2 + 3x) m2, and a classroom, with an area of (2x2 − x + 6) m2. Which expression gives the total area?
items.e: x2-terms: 1 + 2 = 3. x-terms: 3 + (−1) = 2. Constants: 0 + 6 = 6. The total area is (3x2 + 2x + 6) m2. (3x4 + 2x2 + 6 uses x + x = x2, but x + x = 2x.)

items.q: For the food bank drive, Mr. Gill’s class collects (5x + 12) cans and Ms. Chen’s class collects (3x − 4) cans. How many more cans does Mr. Gill’s class collect?
items.e: (5x + 12) − (3x − 4) = 5x − 3x + 12 + 4 = 2x + 16. Subtracting −4 adds 4. (2x + 8 forgets to change the sign of −4. 8x + 8 adds the two amounts.)

items.q: At a Terry Fox Run, a school raises (6x + 25) dollars on Monday, (4x − 10) dollars on Tuesday and (x + 40) dollars on Wednesday. Which expression gives the total?
items.e: x-terms: 6 + 4 + 1 = 11. Constants: 25 − 10 + 40 = 55. The total is (11x + 55) dollars. (11x + 75 ignores the minus sign of 10. 10x + 55 forgets that x is 1x.)

items.q: Mateo drives the Sea-to-Sky Highway. From Vancouver to Squamish is (3x + 5) km and from Squamish to Whistler is (3x − 2) km. How much farther is the first part of the trip?
items.e: (3x + 5) − (3x − 2) = 3x − 3x + 5 + 2 = 7. The x-terms cancel, so the first part is 7 km longer. (3 forgets to change the sign of −2. 6x + 3 adds the two parts.)
